newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee up on high call,low dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee up on high call,low dlr demand.

text.p: High call rates combined with low commercial demand for dollars, to keep the Sri Lanka rupee high, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.65 to the dollar, after opening at 57.80. The rupee closed at 57.73 on Wednesday.
"A lack of import covering saw banks keep away from buying dollars," said an American Express Bank dealer.
Speculators were also silent due to the high cost of holding the U.S. currency, he said.
Overnight call money closed at its opening level of 22 percent, after moving between 17 and 25 percent, dealers said.
"Call rates should ease on Friday, once the market feels the full impact of the Central Bank buying 1.5 billion rupees of Treasury Bills on Wednesday," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
Money became tight when banks covered imports with dollars from the Central Bank for three days from last Thursday.
Wednesday's Treasury Bill auctions were undersubscibed due to the tight money situation, dealers said. Bids received were 3.79 billion rupees, while the amount offered was 4.83 billion.
Average yields on three, six and 12-month bills rose by 0.14 percentage points, 0.03 and 0.19 to 12.63 percent, 14.34 percent and 15.26 percent.
